claim: radar/uradar/sensor/control/ucontrol/ulocate read a fixed number of operands; a line that is one or more operands short leaves the trailing slots at the statement's defaults, so the instruction acts on different values than the ones written.
why: Signature source: tools/instr_semantics.json (radar/uradar/sensor/ulocate `arity`, ucontrol `subcommands[sub].args`); control's per-type operand counts come from Logic-Docs-v1.1.0.md:3038-3140, which prints one written form per type (`control enabled <b> <v> 0 0 0`, `control shoot <b> <x> <y> <v> 0`, `control shootp <b> <u> <v> 0 0`). The analyzer has always trimmed SURPLUS operands (defs_of/uses_of cap at `arity`) and said nothing about a short line, which is how the prompt's own example library shipped `control shoot turret1 target 0` -- four operands for a five-operand signature -- as a shape the gate accepted (out/takeover-20261024/98-quality-analysis.md §3-§4), and how a job could be written into a processor with a turret that never fires. This is deliberately NOT the `op` case: rules/arity-is-not-effective-params.json records that a missing `op` operand is filled by the statement's own default and still compiles to a real OpI (a≠b, `op add r 1`), so op is excluded here -- the warning is only worth making where the operand count decides which value lands in which slot. The engine does not reject a short line: probes on v160.7 (out/_probe_extra.py) show `ulocate` with 3..8 operands parsing to UnitLocateStatement, i.e. the parser fills every missing slot with that statement's default value, so the line still compiles and runs -- it is a wrong-but-running line, not a line the game turns into noop.
